newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai soymeal prices ease as imports arrive.
newsitem.headline: Thai soymeal prices ease as imports arrive.

text.p: Thai soymeal prices are stable to lower this week following the arrival of imports from Argentina and slower short-term demand, traders said on Tuesday.
The price of local soymeal from imported beans was quoted at around 10.40 baht ($0.42) per kg from 10.45-10.50 baht a week ago.

Traders and industry sources predicted that prices would continue to ease as the threat of shortages was removed by a Thai cabinet resolution on Tuesday to abolish import quotas and cut import tariffs on soymeal, soybeans and fishmeal.
The import tariff on corn was also cut to zero from three percent. But the government said corn could be imported only between February 20 and June 30 to protect local farmers.
Three cargoes of low-protein Argentine soymeal arrived at a Thai port on Friday. The price was said to be around US$306-307 per tonne c&f Bangkok.
Traders and industry sources said over 120,000 tonnes of soymeal were expected to arrive between later this month and mid-November.
"I think the government's 1996 low-tariff quota of 830,000 tonnes (of soymeal) was almost covered," one major feed producer said.
"The supply would be enough to meet demand for the rest of the year," she said.
Another trader added that short-term demand had eased as the pig and poultry industry slowed.
But some expected new orders to be placed soon to cover demand early next year.
Indian-origin high-protein soymeal was quoted at US$310-312 c&f Bangkok. U.S. soymeal was quoted at $320-325 and Brazilian below $300.
Corn, meanwhile, was steady as more supply entered the market. But demand also remained active. Feed grade corn was quoted at 4.70-4.75 baht a kg, unchanged from last week.
